title: Conditions Calculated to Destroy
thesis: Article 6(c) of the Rome Statute prohibits inflicting on the group conditions of life calculated to bring about its physical destruction in whole or in part. Track 2 MAID applicants are disproportionately poor, female, and offered minimal housing or income support before being approved for death. Canada has chosen the cheaper option.

scenes.headline: Conditions Calculated to Destroy
scenes.subhead: Death is being offered where housing, income, and palliative care should be.

scenes.unit: of Track 2 MAID recipients reported poverty
scenes.context: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario — Vulnerability and MAiD analysis (2024). Approximately one in three Track 2 recipients reviewed reported poverty as a contributing factor to their suffering. Offers of housing or income support were minimal or absent in most files.

scenes.unit: of Ontario Track 2 recipients were women
scenes.context: Track 2 deaths skew female, poor, and isolated — the demographic profile of persons most exposed to the housing crisis, gendered poverty, and the long-term care collapse.

scenes.unit: Track 2 over-representation in lowest material-resources quintile (vs 20% population baseline)
scenes.context: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, MAiD Death Review Committee — Marginalization Data Perspectives report (companion to 2024 Vulnerability Report). Track 2 recipients are massively over-represented in the lowest material-resources quintile. This is primary statistical evidence that Track 2 operates as a state-administered exit for the materially deprived — relevant to conditions of life calculated to destroy part of a population.

scenes.unit: Track 2 over-representation in highest residential-instability quintile
scenes.context: Same Marginalization Data Perspectives report. Track 2 recipients are nearly half-again over-represented in the highest residential-instability quintile vs the 20% population baseline. The state offers death; it does not offer housing. The number is the indictment.

scenes.speaker: Office of the Chief Coroner of Ontario, MAiD Death Review Committee
scenes.quote: In a substantial subset of Track 2 cases reviewed, the Committee identified that the suffering driving the request was rooted in unmet social needs that the health and social care system had failed to address before the request for MAiD was approved.

scenes.unit: Canadians with access to palliative care at end of life
scenes.context: Canadian Institute for Health Information / Health Canada estimates have repeatedly shown fewer than three in ten Canadians who could benefit from palliative care actually receive it before death — while MAID provisions have grown by double digits every year since 2016.

scenes.headline: Why this satisfies Article 6(c)
scenes.body:
Article 6(c) does not require that the state poison the food supply or burn down the houses. It requires inflicting conditions of life calculated to bring about physical destruction. Denying disabled Canadians the housing, income, and palliative care necessary to live — while simultaneously offering, approving, and funding their deaths — is a calculation. It is on the parliamentary record. It is in the coroner's files.

This is not a budget shortfall. It is a system that has chosen which Canadians get to live and which get an appointment.

scenes.headline: Continue to ACT V
scenes.subhead: Coercion of the Vulnerable — marginalized Canadians being routed into death as the solution to systemic failure.
